1 Preliminary
1.1 Objective and Scope
Considering that the conventional recovery measures of Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) do not
yield desired results for the Financial Service Providers (FSPs) as the FSPs quite often face time-
consuming and costly multiple litigations, resolution of NPLs through restructuring, foreclosure
and write-off are accepted as viable solutions to the problems due to immediate availability of
liquidity for re-utilization, which otherwise is blocked.
Accordingly, in pursuant to Section 202 of the Financial Services Act of Bhutan 2011, the Royal
Monetary Authority of Bhutan hereby adopts the Regulations (Amendment) to provide a
regulatory framework to FSPs to the classify as viable or non-viable, willful or non-willful, provide
restructuring facilities, foreclosing and/or writing-off of NPLs as per the provisions of these
Regulations and the Guidelines (SoPs) of FSPs.
The objectives of these Regulations are to:
a. Reach amicable settlements by protecting the interest of the FSPs and the borrowers
through timely actions/interventions
b. Decongest the books of accounts of the FSPs by foreclosing and/or writing off NPLs;
1.2 Title, Extent and Commencement
These Regulations shall:
a. Be called “Regulations on Non-Performing Loans Management 2025”;
b. Come into force on 1st July 2025; and
c. Apply to Non-Performing Loans of all Financial Service Providers (FSPs).
1.3 Repeal
These Regulations hereby repeals the Rules and Regulations on foreclosure and write-off of Non-
performing Loans 2022, Rules and Regulations for Loan restructuring by Financial Service
Provider(s) 2022, Guidelines on segregation of Non-performing Loans into viable and Non-viable

Loans 2021, SoP for Out of Court settlement of NPLs, Framework for charge off and Transfer of
NPLs to off-balance sheet, SoP for addressing NPLs related to untraceable borrowers, and any
provision of any rules or regulations , directives, which are inconsistent with these Regulations.
2 Segregation of non-performing loans
2.1 Segregation of Non-performing loans into Viable and Non-viable Loans
a. Viable loans are those non-performing loans for which the financial institution foresees a
repayment in future after planning a revised loan repayment schedule with the borrower.
b. For determining viable loans, the following principles shall be followed by the FSPs:

c. Non-viable loans are the type of loans where the FSP does not foresee any loan repayment
even if the loan is revived or rehabilitated. The non-viable loan can be either from willful
defaulter or non-willful defaulter.
2.2 Segregation of Non-viable loans between willful and non-willful defaulters
a. Willful defaulters are those borrowers who have defaulted on their loan repayment
obligations owing to the following reasons/events:
i. The borrower has defaulted in meeting its loan repayment obligation even when
it has the capacity to honor the said obligation. The capacity of the borrower
to honor the obligation shall be assessed by the respective FSPs.
Page 2 of 33

ii. The borrower has not utilized the loan sanctioned for the intended purposes for
which loan was availed but has diverted/siphoned the funds.
iii. The borrower has disposed of or removed the movable or immovable property
given for the purpose of securing the loan without the knowledge of the
financial institution or sold/closed the business against whose income the loan
was sanctioned, without the knowledge of the financial institution.
iv. The borrower has changed contact address and mobile number without
informing the financial institution and refuses to cooperate with Financial
Institution when being followed up on loan overdues or updating of loan
documents.
b. Non-willful defaulters are those borrowers who are unable to meet their loan repayment
obligation due to the occurrence of any of the following events:
i. Complete loss of income from closure of business or not in position to earn any
more income
ii. For events/ situation beyond the borrower’s control.
2.3 Process for Segregation of NPL Loans
a. The process of segregation of NPLs into viable and non-viable loans and then into willful
and non-willful defaulter should be first carried out the by the FSPs.
b. The treatment of viable loans shall be as per the procedures laid in this regulation.
c. The treatment of non-viable loans shall be foreclosed as per the procedures laid in these
regulations.
2.4 Revival and Rehabilitation of Viable Loans
a. The NPL borrowers who meet the criteria of Viable Loans under this guideline shall be
eligible for Loan Revival and Rehabilitation.
b. A debt relief/workout program shall be agreed between the borrower and the FSP under the
rehabilitation program.
c. The debt relief/work out plan shall be termed as ‘Corrective Action Plan’ (CAP).
Page 3 of 33

d. The respective FSP and the borrower shall draw a CAP aimed at improving the cash flow
and profitability of the borrower for meeting the loan repayment obligation as per the
revised repayment schedule.
e. The FSP shall undertake re-assessment of the borrower’s credit worthiness as per
Institution’s credit policies, manual and board directives.
f. The FSP shall form a centralized unit led by Credit head/chiefs for credit re-assessment of
the borrower for revival and rehabilitation.
g. The FSP shall seek approval from respective Institution’s board/ board sub-committee/any
committee constituted by the board based on the delegation of power for revival and
rehabilitation of the viable borrowers.
h. In case of consortium loan, the lead institution shall conduct the credit re-assessment and
the final decision to revive and rehabilitate shall be unanimous among the participating
FSPs.
i. The facilities available under the CAP shall as per Section 3.2 (i) of these regulations.
2.5 Prudent requirement for Revived and Rehabilitated Non-Performing Loans.
a. To enable the FSPs to address/manage the NPL through this regulation, the RMA will
consider exemption on Section 4.5.5 and 4.6.1 to 4.6.5 of Prudential Regulations 2024 and
amended thereof granting the facilities mentioned under Section 3.2 (i).
b. The asset classification of revived and rehabilitated accounts shall remain same as before
since the accounts has to be in ‘Probation of 6 months’ under the new repayment schedule.
c. The accounts can be classified as performing ‘Standard’ only when the repayments term
under the new repayment reschedules have been in-compliance during the probation of 6
months.
d. The provisioning requirement shall be as per Section 4.7 of Prudential Regulation 2024 or
amendment thereof.
2.6 Disclosure and other Requirements
a. To ensure equity and transparency, FSPs shall exercise due diligence, maintain objectivity
and avoid conflict-of-interest in process of reviving and rehabilitating the viable loans.
b. Financial Institution shall develop Standard Operating Procedures for the Centralized unit
for reviving and rehabilitating the viable borrowers.
Page 4 of 33

c. With the implementation of said measures, the performance and other details of all
restructured loans shall be submitted to RMA on a monthly basis in the prescribed format.
d. FSPs shall disclose the details on the Revived and Rehabilitated Loans including the total
number of accounts, amount as part of the notes to its financial statement.

3 Loan Restructuring
3.1 Eligibility of loans for restructuring facility
a. All loans that are in default, which are deemed viable upon fulfillment of the criteria
specified under Section 2.1 of these regulations, shall be eligible for loan restructuring
facility.
b. All performing loans that are experiencing genuine unforeseen financial constraints, shall
be eligible for loan restructuring facility.
c. For providing loan restructuring facility for viable loans which are non-performing, the
FSPs shall assess if the borrower is a willful defaulter or not in line with the criteria
specified under Section 2.2 of these regulations; and
d. A borrower who has been determined as ‘willful defaulter’ shall not be eligible for loan
restructuring facility.
3.2 Process of loan restructuring for loan rehabilitation and revival
a. All loan restructuring shall be carried out by FSPs within 365 days past due.
b. In the event FSP fails to restructure the NPLs, FSP shall initiate the foreclosure process as
per the procedure laid in these regulations under Section 4.2.
c. The FSPs shall conduct loan restructuring affordability assessment of the borrower based
on the borrower’s current and prospective servicing capacity for the loan account.
d. Depending on the nature of the loan, the minimum information and expected
documentation required for FSPs to assess the borrower affordability for availing loan
restructuring facility is specified in Appendix D.
e. Before entering into a loan restructuring facility, the arrangement shall be agreed between
the borrower and the FSP.
f. The FSP shall seek approval from the respective board/board sub-committee/any
committee constituted by the board based on the delegation of power accorded by the board
for loan restructuring. The approving authority shall be independent of the units or
functions involved in carrying out affordability assessment of the borrowers.
g. Among other things, the delegation of authority shall include provisions on limits and
responsibilities related to monitoring of restructured loans.

h. In case of consortium loan, the lead FSP shall conduct the credit assessment including, but
not limited to, review of payment history and the final decision shall be unanimous among
the participating FSPs.

j. Depending on the requirement, the FSPs may allow one or a combination of loan
restructuring facilities for a single loan account at a time to revive or rehabilitate the loan
accounts.
k. Besides the type of restructuring facilities prescribed under Section 3.2. (i), the FSPs may
come up with additional facilities which shall be endorsed by their board of directors and
approved by the Authority.
3.3. Prudent requirement
a. The asset classification of restructured NPL accounts shall remain in the same category for
a period of 6 months. The accounts can be classified as performing ‘Standard’ only when
the repayment term under the revised loan agreement has been regular for 6 months.
b. Any partial repayment (including interest only payment under loan restructuring facilities)
shall not be treated as full repayment to reclassify the loans as performing.
c. The provisioning requirement shall be as per Section.4.7 of Prudential Regulation 2014 or
amendment thereof.
d. FSPs shall be permitted to provide a restructuring facility or facilities mentioned under
Section 3.2. (i), (j) and (k) of these regulations for an account, only once every two years
and not more than two times during the loan tenure.
e. The FSPs shall take strict follow-up measures if borrowers do not comply with the terms
and conditions under the loan restructuring facility such as filling recovery suit within a
month from non-compliance with the revised terms and conditions of the restructured loan.
f. The FSPs shall continue to monitor the restructured loan accounts in-line with the
Regulations on loan origination and monitoring issued by the Authority or any amendments
thereof.
Page 8 of 33

3.4 Disclosure and other Requirements
a. To ensure equity and transparency, an FSP shall exercise due diligence, maintain
objectivity, and avoid conflict-of-interest as per the requirements of Corporate Governance
Rules and Regulations 2024, in the process of loan restructuring.
b. The FSP shall require the officials/members involved in the loan restructuring process to
declare the conflict of interest before attending any meeting on loan restructuring.
c. The FSP shall align its credit policies in-line with these regulations.
d. With the implementation of said measures, the report of all restructured loansshall be
submitted to the RMA monthly in the prescribed format.
e. The FSP shall disclose the details on the total number of accounts and amount as part of
the notes to its financial statement in the annual reports.

4. Foreclosure of Non-Performing Loans
4.1. Pre-litigation Foreclosure
a. When a loan account becomes or shows signs of account becoming NPL such as loans
overdue by more than 30 days or behind an agreed schedule of payment or any events that
will likely impair the borrower’s repayment capacity, the FSP shall follow up with the
borrower to upgrade or maintain the account as performing. Depending on the nature of
the NPL, the recovery process shall be carried out as per FSP’s policies, procedures and
manuals which should be in line with the following:
i. Section 3 of these regulations;
ii. Out of Court Settlement (Refer Appendix A)
iii. Tracing untraceable NPL borrowers (Refer Appendix B); or
iv. Any other relevant directives issued by the Authority from time to time.
b. An FSP shall ensure all follow-ups and negotiations with a borrower are properly
documented with supporting evidence.
c. If a borrower fails to upgrade the NPL to a performing status through the follow-up and
negotiation the FSP shall initiate foreclosure process for the recovery of the loan
outstanding.
d. An FSP shall review and verify the loan documents for any issue of cross-collateralization,
secondary charges, paripasu charges against the collateral/mortgage or when the borrower
is a common borrower among the FSPs. If any issue arises from Section 3.1. (c) above, the
same shall be resolved between the FSP and borrower before moving forward to the next
step.
e. An FSP and non-willful defaulter may choose to enter into negotiation for:
i. Voluntary surrender of the loan security by the borrower for full or partial
settlement of the loan outstanding;
ii. Both the FSP and borrower shall have the right to enter into negotiation for
voluntary surrender or takeover of the loan collateral/mortgage
iii. In the event FSP agrees to accept the security for full settlement of the loan
outstanding, the FSP shall enter into a negotiated settlement with the
Page 10 of 33

borrower/mortgagor and proceed to foreclose the NPL and the NPL account shall
be closed after taking over of the property; and/or
iv. Transfer the NPL to a third party by taking over the security or business from the
borrower.
f. The FSP shall freeze the interest once the physical possession of the loan
collateral/mortgage is taken over by the FSP or based on the court order.
4.2. Foreclosure through Court
a. When an FSP does not foresee any viability to reach a settlement through a negotiation
with the borrower during the pre-litigation foreclosure, an FSP shall initiate recovery
proceedings in the court of law for the foreclosure of collateral/mortgage within 365 Days
Past Due. However, for small-ticket loans, foreclosure through the court may not be
required if a cost-benefit analysis justifies such an approach. The FSP shall adopt a Board-
approved internal policy that specifies the threshold loan amount or outstanding balance
below which court-based foreclosure is not mandatory. In line with this policy, the FSP
may proceed with writing off the loan, waiving the outstanding amount, or taking any other
action, it deems appropriate.
b. An FSP shall stipulate the timeline in its Guidelines within which a recovery suit shall be
filed against the NPL borrower.
c. During the judicial proceedings if a borrower pleads before the court for out-of-court
settlement through negotiation, an FSP may, with the leave of the court, negotiate with the
borrower for the foreclosure of the NPL in question.
d. If a borrower is untraceable for a period of three months despite all reasonable efforts as
per their SoP and the FSP is not able to resolve at its level, the FSP may register cases
against the borrower and request the court to issue a summon order, direct to carry out the
announcement in the media and issue arrest warrants against the untraceable borrower as
per the procedures of the court.
e. If a borrower is still untraceable after exhausting the steps stipulated under Section 4.2.(d),
the FSP may, within a period of one month, request the court to declare the borrower
missing and issue default judgment for the FSP to take over the collateral/mortgage or to
enforce the rights of the FSP to claim its loan outstanding.
Page 11 of 33

4.3. Post-Litigation Foreclosure
a. The FSP shall implement the judgment strictly to the extent possible.
b. The FSP shall exercise the power of sale of the collateral/mortgage through the public
auction or private sale in accordance with the judgment and/or re-enforcement order of the
court as per the provisions of the Guidelines and SoP of FSP.
c. The collateral/mortgage shall be disposed through the public auction through court order.
d. If the FSP cannot dispose of the collateral/mortgage through the public auction or through
the private sale, the FSP may purchase/take over the collateral/mortgage in full or partial
settlement of the loan outstanding as per the OREO policy/policy on treatment of
foreclosed assets
e. In case the proceeds from the sale of collateral/mortgage are insufficient to liquidate the
loan outstanding, the FSP may file a recovery suit for the deficit loan amount in accordance
with Section 52(2) of the Movable and Immovable Property Act of Bhutan 1999 and/or
amendment thereof. The FSPs may waive off the deficit amount as per loan waive off
provisions of these regulations.
f. In case the proceeds from the sale of collateral/mortgage are in excess of the balance
outstanding, the excess/ surplus proceeds from the sale of collateral/mortgage shall be
refunded to the borrower based on the procedures laid in Section 52(1) of Moveable and
Immoveable Property Act of Bhutan 1999 or any amendments thereto.
g. If the FSP is not able to recover the NPL amount through the recovery suit, the FSP shall
write off the balance loan outstanding as per the provisions of these regulations.
5. Observation Period
5.1. Conditions for Observations
a. Observation Period shall not be applicable for NPL accounts closed/ fully repaid through
cash. However, FIs shall put in place proper credit assessment processes to sanction new
loans to these borrowers.
b. The NPLs under the "Substandard" category that have become performing through
repayments of default amount shall subject to observation period of three months from the
date of repayment.
Page 12 of 33

c. If NPL account is closed through court proceedings/foreclosure or transfer of the remaining
loan outstanding to another borrower, the borrower/loan transferor shall be subject to
observation period of six- months from the date of foreclosure or transfer.
d. The NPLs under the "Doubtful" and "Loss" category that have become performing through
repayments made by the borrower shall be subject to six months observation period.
e. The asset classification of NPLs placed under observation period shall remain in the same
category for a period of 3 months even after repayment of the overdue amount. The
accounts can be classified as performing “Standard” only when the repayment has been
regular for 3 months
5.2. Prudent Requirement
a. Non-fund-based facilities such as bank guarantee, letter of credit and other off-balance
sheet exposures shall not be granted to the borrowers classified as non- performing.
However, such facilities may be permitted in exceptional cases, subject to the thorough risk
assessment by the FSP and prior approval from the Authority. The FSP shall submit
comprehensive assessment report, including the rational and risk mitigation measures,
when submitting any such request for approval to the Authority.
b. Renewal of overdraft/working capital may be granted by the FIs but credit facilities should
be renewed within the 90 days (including the past overdue days before the expiry of the
loan) from the date of expiry of the facilities.
c. During the observation period, no borrowers shall be allowed to withdraw the undrawn
amount of the overdraft/working capital from sanctioned amount.
d. The classification of NPLs placed under the observation period shall be as per its respective
loan classification bucket.
e. Financial institutions must have in place processes for monitoring and reporting of loans
classified under the six-month observation period.
f. Independent reviews/audit shall be conducted by the control functions of the financial
institutions to ensure compliance to this Regulations.

6. Write-off of NPLs
6.1. General Process
a. Write-off means removing NPLs from the balance sheet by taking a charge against the
profit and loss account of the FSPs.
b. The loans written-off shall be recorded as an off-balance sheet and FSPs shall continue to
pursue recovery or closure of the NPL.
c. A loan write-off does not forfeit the legal right of the FSPs to recover its loan outstanding
in the future.
d. All loans that have been 100% provisioned and in loss category (loan default by more than
365 days) may be written-off from the balance sheet of FSPs as per the internal policies of
FSP approved by their board.
e. FSP shall write-off the loans only after the commencement of foreclosure through court.
f. The interest and late fees as per the loan agreement shall continue to accrue on the loans
written-off. The FSPs may compute interest and late fee at the end during the loan
recovery/closure.
g. The FSPs shall maintain a proper record and all the relevant documentary evidence of the
written-off loans.
h. The FSPs shall form a dedicated Recovery Unit/Division/assign to existing divisions to
pursue recovery of the written-off loans with clear strategy and targets set by Management
and approved by their Board.
i. The FSPs shall continue submitting the details of the loan written-off to the Credit
Information Bureau (CIB) until the loan outstanding is liquidated/closed.
j. The FSP shall submit a detailed report on the loans written-off to the Authority for
information as part of existing monthly returns.
k. The FSP shall maintain proper internal controls and oversight to ensure that the operational
risk such as process of write-off under these regulations are carried out prudently.
l. The FSP is required to ensure that the loans written off are properly audited by the internal
auditors and the statutory auditors and disclosed in the annual report.
Page 14 of 33

m. The FSP shall seek Authority's written approval before writing off any loans granted to its
related parties. The write off of loans to related parties shall be carried out at an arm's length
basis.
6.2. Prudent Requirement and Accounting Treatment of NPLs Written-off
a. All NPLs written-off shall expense the balance loan outstanding through Profit and Loss/
Income Statement with adjustment against the provisions and interest-in-suspense kept
aside.
b. In case the borrower resumes servicing its loan obligations or the NPL is recovered through
the sale of collateral/mortgage or from the borrower, the recovered amount shall be written
back into the books of the FSP through the profit and loss/ income statement.
c. In the case of a borrower resuming the loan obligations, the account shall be classified as
non-performing category based on its earlier loan classification bucket for a period of 6
months before it can be classified as performing under standard category.
6.3. Conditions to waive the right to recover the NPLs
a. If the FSP does not foresee any recovery of loans written-off, the FSP may waive the right
to pursue further recovery.
b. The FSPs may directly waive off if the loan amount is materially insignificant which are
not economical to pursue further recovery.
c. The FSP shall seek Authority's written approval before waiving any loan or advance
granted to its related parties.
d. The FSP may waive the right to recover written-off loans as per the decisions of the
competent authorities (Courts or Boards of FSPs), subject to fulfillment of the following
conditions corresponding to the respective categories of borrowers:
i. Bankrupt: Bankrupt means that the court through a judgment has declared any
person/ any legal entity bankrupts as per the Bankruptcy Act of Bhutan 1999 or
amendment thereof.
ii. Deceased: Deceased means a borrower who is dead and the same is confirmed
through the death certificate issued by the hospital, Department of Civil Registration
and Census, or local government authority concerned or any other agencies
Page 15 of 33

authorized to issue the death certificate. The deceased has not left behind any
security or property in his name or guarantor to liquidate the NPL. The respective
Boards of FSPs shall confirm and endorse the final list of deceased borrowers.
iii. Imprisonment: Imprisonment means a borrower has been imprisoned by the court
of law either for in lieu of non-repayment of loan/s or for commission of an offence
depending on the imprisonment term, where he does not have any source to repay
the loan/s. The respective Boards of FSPs shall confirm and endorse the final list of
imprisoned borrowers.
e. Those NPLs for which the FSPs have exhausted all measures to recover the NPL or the
Board has passed the resolution to waive the right to recover the NPL after assessing that
the recovery of NPL is not possible.
f. Based on the recommendations of Committee(s) constituted in the FSPs, the right to waive
the recovery of NPL shall be decided/approved by the Boards of FSPs as per the provisions
laid down in the regulations.
g. The Authority may annually verify if an FSPs have carried out the write-off and waive-off
of the rights to recover NPLs as per these regulations.
h. The FSP shall submit a list of waived NPLs to the CIB to ensure that NPLs waived are
included in the borrower’s credit report.
i. The borrower whose loan has been waived shall be barred from getting another loan or
cannot stand as guarantor from any FSP for next 10 years. However, this restriction shall
not apply to Section 4.1.(a)(ii) of these regulations.

7. Definitions and General Provisions
7.1. Non-Performing Loan (NPL): means the loan repayment obligations which are overdue
more than 90 days as prescribed in the Prudential Regulations 2024 and amended thereof.
The non-performing loans includes following features:
a. Role of collateralization: Collateralization or guarantees shall have no direct influence
on the categorization of loan as non-performing.
b. Upgrading to performing: The criteria for reclassifying a non-performing loan as
performing, under the determination of non-performing exposures, shall conform to the
applicable legal framework established by the authority.
7.2. Absconded: Absconded means a person who had left or abandoned the country without
the knowledge of the Royal Government for reasons of corruption charges either due to
corrupt reasons or after having committed anti-national activities or the crime against the
State or Tsawa Sum with sole intent for avoiding judicial process, and whose census has
been deleted from the RGoB records based on the reports of respective local governments.
The final list of absconded borrowers shall be confirmed in writing by the Department of
Law & Order, MoHCA to the FSPs and Authority.
7.3. Authority: means as defined in the RMA Act of Bhutan 2010 or amendment thereof.
7.4. Collateral or mortgage: means movable and immovable properties pledged as the security
against loans as stipulated in the Movable and Immovable Property Act of Bhutan 1999 or
amendment thereof.
7.5. Financial Service Providers (FSPs): means an individual or an entity who/which is given
the registration certificates or licenses by the Authority to provide the financial services to
the public.
7.6. Foreclosure: means a legal process by which an FSP attempts to recover or liquidate the
loan balance outstanding from a defaulting borrower, either through the court order or
through out-of-court settlement in full or partial settlement of the NPLs as approved by the
Boards of FSPs.

waste resources for both the parties. Out-of-court settlement can occur during pre-litigation

7.9. Borrower: An individual either natural or a juridical person, who has entered into a

schedule. In case of borrower with multiple accounts, each NPL accounts shall be assessed

7.11. Viable Loans: Non-performing loans for which the financial institution foresees a
repayment in future after planning a revised loan repayment schedule with the borrower.
7.12. Non-Viable Loans: Non-performing loans where the financial institution does not foresee
any repayments in future.
7.13. Underperforming Business: Business which are facing temporary problems in their
operation due to either mismanagement or policy impact or economic situation.
7.14. Personal loan: Loans which have been availed for personal consumption and shall also
include mortgage loan (loans which are not tied to any specific purpose)
7.15. Business: Licensed commercial establishment for which the borrower has availed the loan
and the repayment is tied with.
7.16. Revival: Improving the financial condition of the borrower for loan repayment obligation.
7.17. Rehabilitation: Process of restoring the borrower’s financial condition for loan repayment

7.18. Diversion of fund: Deploying/ utilizing the borrowed funds for purpose/activities or

Appendix A: Framework for Charge-off and Transfer of NPLs to Off-Balance sheet
1. Background
In line with Section 4, this framework is being designed to clean-up the balance sheet of the FSPs
to ensure that the FSPs can focus on their core business (financial intermediation) and are able to
identify asset quality problems early on through clean balance sheets.
2. Definition & Treatment
2.1. In line with Section 6, write-off is only an accounting term for derecognition/ removal
of the NPLs from the books (balance sheet) of the FSPs and transfer it to off-balance
sheet records.
2.2. To ensure that the term “write- off” does not confuse oversight authorities and the
public as different authorities have different interpretations/ of the term, the RMA will
use the term “charge-off” in lieu of “write-off” until the definitions under Tax law and
RMA Regulation are aligned.
2.3. A charge-off does not preclude the FSP from enforcing and recovering the debt
obligation whereby the borrower still owes the loan outstanding to the FSP as a charge-
off does not entail in forgiving the debt obligation.
2.4. The loans transferred from the books shall be maintained as off-balance sheet assets
which are exposures that could impact the books of the FSPs in the future based on the
possibility/occurrence of an event. For example, the recovery of loans charged-off will
be recognised as income through the profit and loss statement.
2.5. Off-balance sheet exposures include bank guarantees, letter of credit, loans charged-off
or any other contingent assets or liabilities as per BAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Assets
and Contingent Liabilities.
2.6. Off-balance sheet exposures include bank guarantees, letter of credit, loans charged-off
or any other contingent assets or liabilities as per BAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Assets
and Contingent Liabilities.

3.1. As per Section 6.1.(d), fully provisioned loans shall be charged off to ensure the impact
on the books of the FSP are minimal. Charge-off of NPLs is not a double deduction of
expenses as it is only an adjustment of closure of account against the provision kept for
the loans.
3.2. The NPLs shall be Charged-off as:
Provisions xxx (Dr.)
Loan account xxx (Cr.)
3.3. The loan account shall be directly closed from the active loan ledger by debiting the
provisions kept against it through the balance sheet. This is an interim accounting
treatment until the write-off policy of tax and regulator are aligned.
3.4. To ensure that defaulters do not take advantage of the charge off, the FSPs shall
continue to calculate interest and late fees as per the terms and conditions of the contract
in line with Section 6.1.(f), unless the FSPs decides not to charge as per their internal
policies or board approval based on the case circumstances.
3.5. As per Section 4.1.(g) - 4.1.(h), FSP shall maintain records and documents for loans
charged-off with a dedicated division/unit for recovery of those loans.
3.6. To ensure these records are not missed in due course of time and neglected, the FSPs
shall record these loans charged-off in the system (credit software) under separate GL
from the active loans. These records shall be audited by internal audit to ensure that all
loans written off are recorded accurately.
3.7. The system generated loan-charged-off reports and supporting documents should be
available to the RMA, Audit, Tax Authority and any law enforcement agencies
whenever required.
3.8. The FSPs shall continue to recover these charged-off loans through enforcement of its
rights under the terms and conditions of the loan agreement.
3.9. To ensure that the off-balance assets are recovered in a timely manner, the board shall
set targets and strategies on the recovery of those NPLs.

Appendix B: SOP on Out of Court Settlement
1. Background
The out-of-court settlement is being designed for FSPs and loan defaulters to amicably resolve the
existing NPLs through the out-of-court settlement for expediting the NPL resolution with the
objective to relieve borrowers and strengthen the capital and liquidity of the FSPs to prepare for
risks in the future.
Out-of-court settlement (hereafter OCS) is an agreement between FSPs and borrowers to amicably
resolve the NPLs without going to court as litigations are costly and time consuming and waste
resources for both the parties.
Current practices highlight that the borrowers and FSPs still prefer to litigate through court for
foreclosure of NPLs since both the parties do not have incentive to reach the OCS. Therefore, the
standard operating procedures for the OCS is being issued to provide a standard framework for
borrowers and FSPs to amicably resolve the NPLs through OCS.
2. Objectives and Eligibility
2.1. The objectives of this SOPs are to:
a. Provide framework to FSPs for the out-of-court settlement of NPLs.
b. Encourage borrowers and FSPs to amicably resolve the NPLs; and
c. Relieve borrowers from debt burden and strengthen capital position of FSPs through
fast recovery process of NPLs.
2.2. The following categories of NPLs shall be eligible for the OCS:
a. All NPLs parked under the Asset Pending Foreclosure as per Guidelines on Transfer
of NPL Asset, 2020;
b. Any NPLs that have been transferred off-balance sheet for decongesting the books of
accounts;
c. Any NPLs whereby the securities have been seized by the FSPs as per the provisions
of MIPA 1999; and
d. Any other category specified by the Authority from time to time.
2.3. The following NPLs shall not be eligible for OCS:
a. Government/Ministry guaranteed loans;
Page 26 of 33

b. Employee incentive loans; Willful defaulters as per the Guidelines on Segregation of
NPLs into Viable and Non-viable Loans 2021; and
c. Any other category specified by the Authority from time to time.
3. Modality
3.1. The FSPs shall determine the following factors for designing the OCS:
a. The FSP shall review the loan documents and revalue the loan securities to determine
the `MRA" (Maximum Recoverability Amount).
b. The FSP shall break down the total loan outstanding into principal balance, interest
outstanding and late fee/penalty accrued.
c. The FSPs shall compare the MRA and total loan outstanding for settlement of the
NPLs.
d. The portion of total loan outstanding, which is greater than the MRA, the FSPs may
choose to partially write-off the loans to resolve the NPLs through OCS.
3.2. Based on the institution specific NPL experience, the FSPs can design the OCS schemes
as per the following modalities:
a. Option 1: Settlement through liquidation of account
The FSPs shall enter the OCS for liquidation of NPL accounts through repayment by
the client.
b. Option 2: Debt-to-asset swap
The FSPs and borrowers may enter into voluntary surrender agreement of properties
for complete or partial settlement of loan with partial write-off of interest accrued and
late fees to encourage/incentivize OCS. However, if MRA can not cover substantial
part of total loan outstanding under this option, the FSPs may restructure the loan
balance after settlement, with submission of new securities and new execution of loan
agreement between the FSP and the borrower.
4. Accounting and Prudential requirements
4.1. The FSPs shall write-back the provisions of the recovered portion under OCS through
profit and loss accounts or income statement.
Page 27 of 33

4.2. Any partial write-offs shall be adjusted against the existing provisions or interest-in-
suspense kept aside for the NPL account.
4.3. In case the provisions or interest-in-suspense is not adequate to cover the partial write-
offs, the difference shall directly be expensed through profit and loss accounts or income
statement.
4.4. Asset taken over will be booked as "foreclosed assets" under "other assets".
4.5. Any restructured loans from Option 2: Debt-Asset Swap shall be under probation for 6
months before classifying the account as standard.
4.6. The borrower availing OCS scheme shall have settlement history in the CIB report.
5. Implementation
5.1. The FSP shall design their own OCS schemes according to the institution specific NPL
issues and notify RMA with prior approval of their Board.
5.2. The FSP shall provide monthly update on OCS implementation to Authority.
5.3. FSP to train their staffs and prepare for the OCS implementation.
5.4. Any deviation from the SoP issued by Authority shall require prior approval of Authority
through the individual institutions' Boards.
5.5. The FSP shall design FAQs/clarifications to have clear understanding by the borrowers
to facilitate smooth operation of the scheme.
5.6. The OCS facility shall be provided to all eligible borrowers and no favored terms shall
be given to any borrowers.

Appendix C: SOP on tracing untraceable NPL borrowers
1. Background
In line with the resolution adopted during the second National High-Level Committee meeting
held on 3rd February 2021 for the resolution of non-performing loans, the Standard Operating
Procedure (SOP) is being issued to assist the Financial Service Providers in tracing the untraceable
borrowers with non-performing loan accounts and treatment of NPLs thereof.
2. Untraceable Borrower
2.1. As per Guidelines on Foreclosure and Write Off of NPLs, an Untraceable/missing borrower
means a borrower who has been at large and the FSP ’s recovery procedure has been fully
exhausted (through media announcement, issue of arrest warrant by the Court and the
police has confirmed in writing that the said borrower is untraceable/missing from Bhutan).
The respective Boards of FSPs shall confirm and approve the final list of
untraceable/missing borrowers and share the same with the RMA.
2.2. Considering the present issues of untraceable borrower at different levels such as arrest
warrant issued by the court or still in process being tracked by the Financial Institutions,
the SOP is developed with the intent to provide a uniform approach in tracing the borrowers
within the existing legal framework and address the NPLs arising from such issues.
3. Different Level of Tracing the borrower
3.1. Level 1: Tracing the borrower at Financial Institution level
a. As and when the loan account becomes NPL or is behind the agreed repayment
schedule as per the terms and conditions of Loan Agreement, the FSPs shall follow
up with borrowers for loan repayment.
b. If the borrower cannot be located or contacted due to change in contact address and
contact number, the FSPs shall carry out the following to confirm the borrower’s
whereabouts:
i. Contact witness/s who have signed on the loan documents;
ii. Contact local government/s; and
Page 29 of 33

iii. Request family contact details from Department of Civil Registration and
Census, MOHCA.
c. The FSPs shall document and maintain record specified under 9.3.2.
3.2. Level 2: Tracing the borrower through the court’s intervention
a. If FSPs are still not able to trace the borrowers through the steps stipulated under
Level 1, the FSPs shall request legal interventions from the court/s.
b. The FSPs shall submit the written documents as evidence to substantiate that the
FSPs has exhausted all steps from Level 1, to the court/s.
c. The FSPs shall request the intervention from the court/s to locate or trace the
borrower through issue of court order for the following:
i. Requesting mobile numbers from telecommunication service providers based on
CID; and
ii. Media announcement of asking clients to report to Financial Institutions and the
media expense will be borne by the FIs.
d. If the borrower fails to report as per steps in 9.4.3, the FSPs shall request court/s to
issue arrest warrant against the borrower.
3.3 Level 3: Declaring the borrower as missing/untraceable
If FSPs are still not able to locate or contact the borrowers through the interventions from Level 2,
then the Financial Institution shall request the court/s to declare the borrower as missing and
request court to allow FSPs to register case for default judgement to take over the mortgaged
properties or enforce the rights of the FSP when the borrower is found.
3.3. Transfer of NPL Asset, write-off and accounting treatment
a. Once the borrower has been declared missing, the FSP shall write-off the NPLs as
per these regulations.
b. The FSPs shall take note that write-off means only removing bad loans from the
books of accounts and shall not entail in forgiveness of debt as per these regulations.
c. The accounting treatment for write-offs shall be in line these regulations.
